messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Public-facing terminology map for transfers & subprocessors — review

Hey team,

Quick one — sales keeps getting ad-hoc questions from prospects (most recently Acme Cloud) asking us to explain: 1) what we mean by "data transfers" across borders, 2) who a "subprocessor" is in our DPA, and 3) what customers can expect when we add or change subprocessors. Legal has already given the formal definitions, but we need a short, customer-friendly set of snippets for three places: the hosted API privacy modal, the console tooltip, and a single-paragraph FAQ for procurement.

I've attached a working draft (Redwood_Public_Terminology_Map_v0.3.docx) with three candidate phrasings per item: a one-sentence definition, a 1–2 sentence explanation with example, and a one-line sales snippet. Can you each review the parts relevant to you: 
- Kimberly: legal accuracy + anything that could trigger contract redlines
- Laura: tone/length for console + sales snippets (we want <120 chars for tooltip)
- Priyom: dev docs/links we should point to (audit log, DPA)
- Rishi: anything we should avoid saying for EU customers (data residency sensitives)

Goal: finalize safe, publishable language by end of week so we can push into the hosted API privacy modal and a short sales KB.

Notes / flagged items in the doc:
- "Transfer" vs "cross-border transfer" — customers want plain phrasing, legal wants precision
- Subprocessor notification cadence: marketing-friendly language vs strict contract wording

Thanks — attaching the draft and Acme's security questionnaire they sent (stub).

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com

Attachments:
- Redwood_Public_Terminology_Map_v0.3.docx (draft glossary; 3 candidate phrasings per term)
- ACME_Security_Questions_Q120_stub.pdf (excerpted questions relevant to terminology)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Public-facing terminology map for transfers & subprocessors — review

Thanks, Nikhil — quick legal read. I made inline suggestions in the attached draft but call out two items here because they affect what we can publish without a policy update:

1) "Subprocessor" short line: we can use "service providers we engage to process data on your behalf" as the tooltip; it is consumer-friendly and consistent with the DPA. Avoid "third-party vendors" in the tooltip because that can be read more broadly.

2) Notification cadence: we cannot promise a specific "30 day notice" text unless Legal updates the DPA language (we currently say "prior notice where feasible"). For the sales KB we can use: "We notify customers before adding a new subprocessor where required by contract or regulation." That is actionable for sales without overcommitting.

Minor: prefer "cross-border transfer" to "data transfer" in EU-facing copy, then explain in parentheses what that means (e.g., moving data between countries).

I'll mark the exact suggested strings in the doc and flag anything that would require DPA/TOU changes.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance

Nice draft, Nikhil — I pulled a few suggested UI-length variations into the doc. A couple of practical notes from Console/Docs POV: 

- Tooltip constraints: aim for <=100 characters; we should use the short legal-approved phrase Kimberly suggested and then link to the full two-sentence explainer in the modal. Example tooltip: "Subprocessor: a service provider we engage to process your data." (87 chars)
- FAQ for procurement: make the first line explicitly state what customers can do (e.g., "You can request export logs, subprocessor list snapshots, and data residency options"). Then link to DPA and the marketplace page.
- For the hosted API privacy modal, include a small "last updated" timestamp and a link to the subprocessor registry (automated feed).

I pushed the UI copy into the Drive link (see related_links). I also shortened the sales snippet suggestions so AE's can paste into follow-ups without legal heavy-lifting.

—Laura

Sara — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers below and next steps: 

1) One-paragraph FAQ (copy you can paste):

"How does Redwood handle cross-border transfers?"
"Redwood may process and route data across countries to provide low-latency inference. When customer data is transferred across borders from the EEA to countries without an adequacy decision, we rely on appropriate safeguards such as standard contractual clauses (SCCs) or equivalent mechanisms, as reflected in our DPA. Contact your account rep if you need a copy of the executed SCCs for your account."

2) Subprocessor list: we publish a near-real-time registry in the console ("Data Processors" -> "Subprocessors") and we can provide a snapshot export for procurement. Laura will add a direct link to the registry in the hosted API privacy modal.

Next steps: Kimberly will finalize the short legal-safe lines in the attached doc; Laura will drop the tooltip + modal copy into Drive and Priyom will wire the modal link to the registry. Rishi — can you confirm whether we should avoid the word "SCCs" in the customer FAQ for EU public pages or keep it but expand to "standard contractual clauses (SCCs)"?

I'll attach the draft FAQ in the Drive link and will prepare a single-page sales KB we can give procurement teams.

Thanks all — aiming to ship the modal copy + registry link by close of week.

—Nikhil
